oracle.cross_check: scipy==1.18.1 scipy.stats.entropy: sum_y p(y)[H(G)-H(G|y)] agreed with dit's I(G;Y) to 1e-13 on every case
oracle.algorithm: I(G;Y) = sum_g p(g) sum_y p(y|g,d) [H(G)-H(G|y,d)] on the joint law of graph and observation
oracle.note: Every expected_information_gain below was produced by running the pinned released dit package on the recorded posterior, features and reliabilities in a temporary environment that was deleted after import: this version of dit, with these inputs, produced this output.

generation.env: uv venv <tmp>/eigenv --python 3.12 && VIRTUAL_ENV=<tmp>/eigenv uv pip install dit && <tmp>/eigenv/bin/python eig_dit_harness.py
generation.resolved_dependencies: numpy==2.5.3, scipy==1.18.1, networkx==3.7, xarray==2026.9.0, boltons==26.2.0, debtcollector==3.1.0, lattices==0.5.1, pltable==1.1.0, loguru==0.7.3, pandas==3.0.6

normalization.observation_channel: p(y|g) = reliability*1[y = feature(g)] + (1-reliability)/category_count; reliability 0 is uninformative, 1 is perfect
normalization.information_gain: expectation is taken before any non-negativity check; individual entropy reductions are not clipped
